O beloved, a garland of a thousand jewels should be worn on all parts of the body;
its wearing is like that of rudrākṣas, and it is purified by the mantra of Kālī. (29)
The rosary is said to be of three kinds: superior, middling, and inferior;
namely, one made of teeth, one made of seeds, and one with a central bead (meru) formed by the upper incisor.
The supreme garland is said to be the supreme attractor of Kālī;
that which resides between the ear and the eye is celebrated as the Great Conch (Mahāśaṅkha). || 31 ||
A garland made of great conch shells consisting of fifty beads is declared to be the medium-sized garland; it is prescribed for the recitation of the Tārā mantra.
Whether made of bones or human skulls, or even one fashioned from human foreheads, a garland worn upon the body or situated on another's body is called the *kiniṣṭhikā* garland. 33.
O Goddess, in the ritual of Chinnādevī, it is thus considered to be threefold;
those two teeth which face each other are proclaimed as the "royal teeth" (rājadanta).
In ancient times, the Dānavas were devoured by Mahākālī of the formidable mouth;
her two tusks, which dwell in the three worlds, are known as the Rājadantas. (35)
O beloved, the name "Rājadantā" was indeed previously given to the goddess by me,
for those two teeth of mine which chew the Daityas are both effective in their task.
Therefore, with a joyful mind, they were appointed to the task of Meru;
and another view is proclaimed in the Kālikā-saṃhitā. (37)
O Maheśānī, because the face of the Goddess shines by means of that tooth,
for that reason, O Goddess, it is celebrated as Rājadanta (the Royal Tooth).
Listen to another: among the teeth, the *rājadantaka* shines;
one should diligently fashion a garland with the threads of the sun, fire, and moon. (39)
Whether by means of fat, marrow, or even by means of women, that channel which was spoken of by Svayambhū is considered auspicious; that channel is the most excellent of all.
The sūtra spoken by Svayambhū is the most excellent of all sūtras;
likewise, there is the sūtra fashioned by a courtesan and that fashioned by a maiden.
Then [he should offer] that which is fashioned by the meritorious wives of the best of the twice-born, as well as that which is free from knots,
smeared with *kuṇḍa*, smeared with *go*, and likewise smeared by the Self-born One.
Then, O beloved, having obtained that which is the most excellent of all from the hand of Mātaṅginī,
one should perform the threading with a needle using a red cloth.
This garland, however, bestows accomplishment and effects the summoning of Kālī;
she who is Kālī is indeed Tārā, and she who is Tārā is indeed Kālī. (44)
She who is Kālī is indeed Chinnā; she who is Chinnā is indeed Tāriṇī.
She who is Sundarī is indeed Kālī, and she is considered the bestower of all accomplishments (siddhis). (45)
There is no distinction between the four; one who makes a distinction shall go to hell.
A rosary, a vessel, and a seat are considered auspicious for all four.

O Pārvatī, there is a distinction in the mantra and meditation, as well as a contradiction regarding the name; furthermore, there is a distinction in the ritual application and other details specifically in the case of Sundarī.
There is no distinction between these three; she is celebrated as the Triple Power (Triśakti).
And Kālikā always dwells in the external cremation grounds.
Therefore, the heroic posture (vīrāsana) is praised, as is the heroic accomplishment (vīrasādhana);
likewise, rites such as the heroic posture constitute the heroic accomplishment. || 49 ||
It is said that [the ritual] includes the mantra, the bali offering, and the binding of the directions;
a corpse with its limbs unbroken is praised, while one with broken limbs is called "muṇḍa."
O Goddess of gods, if it is stained with blood, then it must be discarded with great effort;
O Goddess of gods, if through negligence the practitioner does not discard it, [the following occurs].
At that very moment his death occurs; otherwise, it is indeed auspicious.
Thus, O Goddess, this has been told in brief by the command of Lava.
Now, listen with diligence to the rites such as the Vīrasiddhi and others. 52.

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Seats," in the second section of the northern part of the *Śrīśaktisaṅgamamahātantrarāja*, within the dialogue between the venerable Akṣobhya and Tārā. || 9 ||
The Tenth Chapter.
The venerable Śiva said: Now, therefore, I shall fully describe the supreme Vīrasiddheśvarī.
By the mere knowledge of which one becomes equal to Mahākāla. || 1 ||
O Śivā, [the attainments are] the wooden sandals, the sword, the vetāla, alchemy, the yakṣiṇī, the pill, the collyrium, the accomplishment, protection, and the forehead mark.
Everything is quickly possible; otherwise, the word of Śaṅkara would not be so.
Kālikā, Tāriṇī, and Chinnā are declared to be the triple power (triśakti).
O Goddess, this practice concerning the three powers has been proclaimed;
it is named the "Worship of the Skull" (Muṇḍakopāsana) and bestows all spiritual accomplishments.
She whose form is the embodiment of the *sādhanā* is known as Muṇḍadurgā;
she [slays] Raṇavīra, Mahāvīra, and likewise those who have their throats bound by nooses.
Those impaled on spears, those pierced by staffs, those struck by the thirty-six weapons, those whose lives were lost to serpents and the like, and those torn apart by elephants and tigers; || 6 ||
O Goddess Pārvatī, having brought corpses of those who died of untimely death,
you diligently constructed a fortress with great heroes and great headless trunks.
O Śivā, beginning from Raṇavīra and ending with Mahāvīrāntaka,
one should construct a circle of severed heads (muṇḍadurgaka) all around for the purpose of providing seats.
One should perform [the rite] at Muṇḍadurga with fifteen thousand, eight thousand, seven thousand, six thousand, five thousand, or, in their absence, three thousand repetitions.
O Pārvatī, having drawn the wheel of the form of Tārā before oneself,
[one should do so] for the sake of the vessel, for one's own sake, and also for the sake of the deity, O Pārvatī.
Having abandoned bathing with effort, one should accomplish the practice of the Durgā-mantra in a fortress,
a forest, the middle of a river, a pond, or an empty house.
O Goddess of the gods, [one should practice] in battle, in a cremation ground, at a triple-path or a quadruple-path,
at a family tree or a solitary tree, or else in a temple of Śiva.
With effort, one should master Muṇḍadurga at Ekaliṅga;
O Goddess, when that one is mastered, the three worlds are mastered.
O Pārvatī, having placed the requisites for the *vīrasādhana* before him, one who is dressed as a hero and endowed with compassion [should take] stakes made of *khadira* wood and *ānandaśakti*. (14)
Having carefully performed both the internal and external bindings, O Pārvatī, and having completed everything with diligence as in the Vīrasādhana, O Pārvatī. (15)
O Supreme Goddess, as long as these shaven heads arrive here,
they become beloved through the sequence of the ten Vidyās.
Kālī, Tārā, as well as Chinnā, Sundarī, and Bagalāmukhī—these five will especially become his favorites in an instant. (17)
Whatever offering is requested by them, each and every one should be given with great effort;
a boon should be received with diligence by those who worship the Vīra-yantras. 18.

O Śivā, a man who remains for a moment at Muṇḍadurga, chanting the Vīra-mantra, using a vīra-vessel, and sitting upon a vīra-garland, attains the supernatural powers (siddhis) of the three worlds. || 19 ||
Having treated fear as if it were a blade of grass, the great hero clad in the directions alone shall become a man in the form of Śiva; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
Through the yoga of the five *ghaṭīs* in the yoga of universal sovereignty, the five desired ones will become embodiments of the Great Vidyās. || 21 ||
They will bestow desired accomplishment and all perfections at every moment;
O Goddess, they must be kept secret by a practitioner who desires his own welfare in the Kali age. 22.
O Tāriṇī, this sādhana is to be kept secret like one's own birth;
it is the sovereignty of the three worlds, a sublime poem, and an art that holds great sacred knowledge.
The power of the curse is fierce; the fruit arises from Muṇḍadurga.
Then [one should draw] a dot, a triangle, and the sun, adorned thereafter by an eight-petaled lotus.
A circle joined with a square and adorned with eight vajras;
a dot (bindu) the color of vermilion, and a triangle of divine color.
The sun is the color of saffron, and on its petals are the eight syllables; the circle is the color of Kālikā, and the outer square (bhūpura) is white in color.
The wheel of the sovereignty of Tārā has four castes and four gates;
it is enriched with the ornamentation of eight tridents, and within its three triangles are the three Śaktis.
O Great Goddess, the seed-syllables (bījas) corresponding to their respective colors are Kāmeśī, Diksureśvarī, and Pracaṇḍā; thereafter, Mahākālī is on the petal.
Rudrāṇī, Ugrā, Ghorā, Bhīmā, Ambikā, and Mahārātribhairavī; following these is the group of eight Vairocanas. (29)
Padmāntaka and the others are to be worshipped; one should worship Kullaka upon the head.
One should worship Akṣobhya there, and everything else as before. (30)
Having thus fashioned the wheel consisting of Kālī, one should perform the sādhana;
[placing] four practitioners at a distance, who are like sacrificial posts (svaru) and situated in a remote location. || 31 ||
"O Goddess, having performed [the rite], one should accomplish it; what is there that is not as good as being held in the hand?
Thus has it been told in brief; what else do you wish to hear? (32)
The Goddess said: "O Lord of Gods, I wish to hear that which is the most secret of secrets.
Śrī Śiva said:
Kālī, Tārā, as well as Chinnā, and Sundarī is considered the fourth. || 33 ||
In this manner, one should perform the heroic practice (*vīrasādhana*) within the ten sciences (*vidyā*):
namely, in the Śaiva, Gāṇapatya, Cāndra, Bauddha, and likewise in the Svāyambhuva [Tantras]. (34)
O Goddess of the gods, one should perform the heroic practice (vīrasādhana) within these: the Vaiṣṇava, Saura, Gāruḍa, and Kerala mantras. (35)
O Śivā, one should not perform the rite of *vīrasādhana* in the Vedic tradition;
nor, O Goddess of Devas, should one perform *vīrasādhana* even in Kerala.
O Goddess, one may practice even according to Vedic injunctions if such be the intention;
O Goddess, one may practice even in Kerala if it be cruel or foolish.
The primary means of accomplishment is proclaimed for both Kālī and Tārā;
she who is Kālī is indeed Tārā, and this is likewise accepted for Chinnamastā. (38)

In this manner, one should perform the heroic practice (vīrasādhana) among the Pāśupata and other [sects], and one should perform the heroic practice among the Vidyās such as Bagalā and others. || 39 ||
One who desires success while abandoning the rite of heroic accomplishment (vīrasādhana) is like one who wishes to see a form in a mirror without eyes. || 40 ||
Therefore, O Pārvatī, among the ten Vidyās, the primary means of accomplishment is Tāriṇī, who is the form of Brahman; she is Kālikā, the beautiful one of Brahman.
Chinnā and the others are the perfection of Brahman; Sundarī is the dense mass of the consciousness of Brahman.
Thus, O Mistress of the Gods, the state of Brahman remains pervading everywhere.
She possesses preeminence among all sciences; even there, O Goddess, she is Kālikā in the Kali age.
O Śivā, she is of one, two, or three kinds, and is tenfold and hundredfold.
O Goddess, she who possesses infinite forms appears as Lakṣadhā and Koṭidhā; through her various limbs and distinct names, she is celebrated as Kālikā.
The primordial power Kālikā is herself Tārā and Kullukā;
she is also celebrated as Sundarī, Chinnamastā, and indeed as Kālikā alone. (45)
For as long as she can be described, she possesses qualities;
when she becomes beyond the reach of words, then she has become devoid of qualities.
O Maheśvarī, even with thousands of crores of tongues and hundreds of crores of mouths, I am unable to describe her greatness.
When its impossibility [of being described] arose, at that very moment Brahman was proclaimed;
for what indeed is "being devoid of qualities" other than falling within the scope of the inability to describe it? (48)

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Discourse on Vīrasiddheśvarī," in the second section of the Uttarabhāga of the *Śrīśaktisaṅgamamahātantrarāja*, within the dialogue between the venerable Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā. || 10 ||
The eleventh chapter.
The venerable Śiva said:
Thus has the state of being devoid of qualities (nirguṇatva) been proclaimed; what else do you wish to hear?
Śrī Kālī said:
O Ādinātha Mahākāla, bestower of boons, who acts for the welfare of all beings! (1)
The ten Mahāvidyās were heard by him directly;
the ten Laghu-mahāvidyās are likewise proclaimed to be ten in number.
Thirteen great vidyās were proclaimed by Virūpākṣa, and likewise sixteen vidyās were revealed by Bhairava. (3)
O Goddess, O Deity, Mahāvidyā is also known as Siddhavidyā;
she is called Triśakti, O Lord, and Triśakti is considered to be threefold.
Kālī, Tārā, and Chinnamastā are proclaimed as the Triśakti; O God, Bālā, Pañcadaśī, and Ṣoḍaśī are likewise remembered as the Tririti.
The glory of the three powers is proclaimed when [the world] is severed;
everything previously mentioned has been recounted by you there as well.
O Supreme Lord, whatever is generally most secret,
O God— even more secret than the secret— tell that to me today.
Īśvara said:
O Pārvatī, among the hymns of a thousand names and also within the armor-rites (kavacas), that armor and so forth have been proclaimed; indeed, that preparatory rite (puraścaraṇa) must be performed.
Where no preliminary rite (puraścaryā) is mentioned, what indeed is prescribed there?
For ten thousand recitations (ayuta) are proclaimed as the preliminary rite for a mere hymn (stotra). || 9 ||
This is considered the preliminary rite (puraścaryā) for the armor of the thousand names;
having thus performed the preparatory service, one should perform the fire-oblation and other rites consisting of a tenth part [of the recitation].
O Goddess, libation (tarpaṇa) and purification (mārjana) are proclaimed in some places; according to the opinion of Mahākāla, one should perform them if they are situated there. 11.
O beloved Pārvatī, one should by all means provide a meal for the brāhmaṇas at the conclusion; indeed, through the complete satisfaction of the brāhmaṇas, everything is accomplished.
O Supreme Goddess, how should the fire-oblation be performed, and what should the preliminary ritual (puraścaryā) be like? And of what nature is the Thousand Names? (13)
(44) Likewise, O Goddess, what form is proclaimed for the armor?
The dialogue between Śiva and the Goddess is proclaimed as [the section on] the Brahmarandhra. 14.
Other verses are equal to hair; the seer is said to be Śiva; O Goddess, the meter is the mouth, and the deity is the heart. (15)
The seed-syllable (bīja) is declared to be the secret, while power (śakti) is considered to be the supreme;
O Goddess, the conceptualization of all the limbs is proclaimed as mere figurative praise (arthavāda). || 16 ||
Whatever exists within the midst of a hymn, all that is of the nature of a hymn;
and thus, O Goddess of the gods, it is proclaimed to be the very form of a hymn. (17)
O Goddess, O Beloved, one should recite that very armor-mantra from the beginning to the end; O Supreme Goddess, if it be deficient in its limbs, there will surely be destruction in every respect.
O Goddess, the fruit resulting from praise and so forth is designated as "Gati.
O Goddess, excluding the beginning and the end, it is proclaimed that the fruit is half [of what it would otherwise be]. (19)
O Goddess, regarding this matter, how is the conviction established by the five limbs and so forth as they are traditionally remembered?
O Goddess, how should the fire-oblation be performed—should it be at the end of each verse, or is there an oblation for the entire hymn?
Now listen with diligence to the fire-offering (havana) for the armor-mantra (kavaca) and the others;
it is taught that one should perform the offering after reciting [the mantra] from beginning to end.
"Alternatively, O Goddess of the gods, it is held that the oblation should be performed at the end of the name.
The Śrī Devī said:
"If the oblation is to be at the end of the name, how could it be during the introductory invocation (upoddhāta)? (22)
O Supreme Lord, how should the armor-mantra be employed at the beginning of the armor-rite? Should it end with the name [of the target], or should it conclude with a verse? (23)
"Or it may be performed in its entirety during the rite of oblation, O Śaṅkara.
Īśvara said:
"O Goddess, according to the opinion of Sāṅkhyāyana, the procedure for the Gauḍa recension is considered authoritative."
O Maheśvarī, the names that are to be recited are those situated in the middle;
[one may recite] half a verse, or even just a quarter, or half a quarter, or merely the name itself. (25)
O lady of excellent vows, one should recite the *Nāmasāhasra* with effort while remaining impartial;
this is declared to be the tradition of Sāṅkhyāyana. Listen now to the introduction, O beloved. (26)
The introduction and the conclusion are considered to be the invocation at the end of the verse;
one should perform the invocation at the end of that, so said Sāṅkhyāyana. (27)
O Dear One, even in the case of the armor-mantra (kavaca) and others, the oblation (havana) should occur at the end of the mantra;
it is held that at the beginning and conclusion [of a section], the oblation occurs at the end of the verse.
O Maheśvarī, having first recited it in its entirety and likewise at the end, the names should be recited in the middle; this is proclaimed as *puraścaryā*.
O Goddess, now listen with diligence to the sequence known as Kāśmīraka;
having recited the hymn in its entirety, one should perform the counting at its conclusion. (30)
The yoga of the complete sequence is proclaimed as that which is called Kāśmīra;
and the yoga of the complete fire-oblation has been described, O Priyaṃvadā. (31)
O Maheśvarī, one should perform the rites of cleansing and consecration here;
however, O Pārvatī, there is some difference in the regions known as Kāśmīra and Kerala.
In this very same sequence, the fire-offering (homa) for the armor (kavaca) is prescribed;
or rather, the wise man should diligently perform the libations (tarpaṇa) and other rites for the armor.
Sārūpya is called Kavaca, while Sāyujya is said to be the Stotra;
the Sānnidhya is the Sahasranāma—this triad is thus proclaimed. (34)
O Goddess, speech accompanied by light is praise; therefore, the wise person should recite it in its entirety.
O Great Goddess, this very [method] is also proclaimed in Kerala. (35)
This has been declared for the mere recitation of the text; however, it is prescribed for the fire-oblation (homa) and other rites.
In the Kāmarūpāgama, it is stated that after the oblations at the end of the world-section, one should recite the armor (kavaca).

When the name "Kāmarūpāgama" is accepted as being fashioned by Akṣobhya, the oblation is prescribed at the end of the world (loka), and the cleansing and other rites at the end of the verse (śloka). || 37 ||
Then, one should perform the preliminary rites (puraścaryā) and so forth according to the procedure taught in the Tantras;
the armor (kavaca) shall take the form of armor, and the hymn (stotra) shall become one's companion.
The *Sahasranāmastotra* is proclaimed for the location of the army; worship is of the nature of Durga, while the offering of the sacrificial oblation (*bali*) is the act of slaying. (39)
The preliminary practice (*puraścaryā*) of the king of mantras is said to be the attainment of sovereignty;
for without such attainment, O Maheśvarī, a king does not shine. (40)
For all this is proclaimed to have its root in prosperity;
the fire-oblation is called the Agni-missile, while the libation is the Parjanya-missile.
The nature of the fortress in the water is proclaimed to be the consecration (abhiṣeka), while the feeding of the Brāhmaṇas is the devouring of the wicked army. || 42 ||

Having meditated upon the identity of the deity, the guru, and the vidyā as being one with oneself, and having become a master of all accomplishments (sarvasiddhi), one shall become the sovereign of the three worlds. || 43 ||
And just as there may be fear of an enemy army in the case of kingship and the like, O Great Goddess, so too has the attainment of the kingdom of siddhi been described. (44)

O Goddess, just as the construction of fortresses, weapons, and so forth is considered essential for the kingdom of the gods, even so are the preliminary rites (*puraścaryā*) and other such practices considered essential for the sovereignty of spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*). || 45 ||
The mantra is the king, the guru is the minister, Gaṇeśa is the gatekeeper;
the practice with a corpse and a skull is declared to be the throne. (46)
The practitioner should act in such a way that everything is successfully accomplished;
both the occasional (naimittika) and the optional (kāmya) rites are considered to be performed by means of horses and elephants.
The smoke of the fire-oblation shall be its banner, and the tantra is the ground for accomplishment; O Goddess, when there is mastery over the lord of ghee, what on earth is not accomplished?
The sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa) and other rites constitute the army that bestows the sovereignty of the deity;
the Yantra is indeed the adamantine fortress, while the Bījayantro is indivisible.
The preliminary ritual (puraścaryā) for the armor (kavaca) and other mantras has been declared; what do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Preliminary Rite of the Armor and Other Practices," in the second section of the latter part of the *Śrīśaktisaṅgamamahātantrarāja*, in the dialogue between the venerable Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā. || 11 ||
The Twelfth Chapter.
The Goddess said: O Lord of Gods, I desire to hear the definitive explanation of the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
The illustrious Śiva said: Indeed, there are three kinds of purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), according to the Keralādi sequence and so forth. || 1 ||
One should perform the purification of the body through the fivefold purification of the principles (tattva).
Thus has the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) been described by me to you in Kerala.
In Kashmir, however, the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) proceeds by way of the sequence of drying and so forth;
O Goddess, when the pervasion of the principles (*tattva*) has been accomplished, what sin could possibly exist upon the surface of the earth? (3)
O Maheśvarī, through the application of the sequence of withdrawal, there is the pervasion of the principles (tattvas).
O Goddess, when this sequence is performed in this manner, where can his sin remain? (4)
O Goddess, through the purification of the elements, even his sin departs;
since sin resides in the body, where else could that sin exist? (5)
O Great Goddess, when the pervasion of the principles (*tattva*) has been accomplished, one should contemplate "I am indeed Brahman.
Then, for the sake of the pervasion of the *mātṛkās*, one should take recourse in the purification of the body.
O Goddess, O Śivā, through the sequence beginning with drying, sin residing in the elements is [removed];
once the purification of the elements has occurred, O Maheśvarī, where is there any sin? (7)
The Krama known as Kāśmīra has been proclaimed; the Gauḍa [Krama] should be like the Kāśmīra.
O Goddess, O beloved, listen now to the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) in the Krama called Caitanya.
O Pārvatī, having performed the enumeration of the principles (tattvas) through the yoga of the process of withdrawal,
one should diligently perform the rite for the purification of sins.
One should perform the rites of drying and so forth by means of the yoga of the sequence of withdrawal (saṃhāra).
O Goddess of the Gods, for that which is of the nature of sin, stability indeed occurs through the path of emanation (sṛṣṭi).
O Goddess, one should again perform the creation and other rites by way of emanation, so that creation, maintenance, and so forth may occur at the beginning of the age, O Goddess. || 11 ||
In the same way, O Supreme Goddess, the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) has been proclaimed.
O Pārvatī, where indeed does this transmigratory world of moving and non-moving beings go? (12)
In the same way, O Goddess of Gods, the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), as well as meditation and yoga,
and likewise the various divisions of creation, are established from time immemorial.
O Maheśānī, the nine Āgamas are honored as the modifications (Vaikṛtis);
they are known by the designation of Purāṇas, O Śivā, and through them all perfection shall be attained.
O Goddess of the gods, that supreme *kalā* known as Kālikā, relying upon the door of the One, illumines this entire world of the moving and the unmoving. (15)
O Maheśvarī, that power which, having bound those who are wounded by the snare of Māyā, causes them to wander in the wheel of saṃsāra, O Queen of the Gods. (16)
O Maheśvarī, in the case of Śrīvidyā, Kālī, and the Ūrdhvāmnāya,
by the mere sight of him, the sin of another departs.
That region extends for ten million yojanas in every direction and attains blessedness;
O Goddess, I am unable to describe the fruit of its merit.
Thus it has been briefly declared: O Maheśvarī, whence can there be sin for one who performs the recitation (pārāyaṇa) of the Ṣoḍaśī and likewise of Kālikā? (19)
O Goddess, [there is] the mastery of mantras, as well as the mastery of names;
O Goddess, the mastery of the wheel, and likewise the mastery of the yantra.
O Goddess, they know the *nāḍīpārāyaṇa* as the fifth *pārāyaṇa*;
[this occurs] through the sequence of the five *pārāyaṇas* in the Śrīvidyā and the Kālikā [traditions].
The twilight rite is called *pārāyaṇa*; by it, indeed, no sin exists.
In the state of liberation (*nirvāṇa*), there is no mention of sin; O Śivā, one should speak of what precedes the Supreme.
O Great Goddess, O Goddess, through the practice of the sequence of the six cakras in the Ṣaṭśāmbhava [system], sin is cast far away; indeed, it is the purification of those who are solitary. (23)
One should likewise conceive of the purification of prosperity for others as being threefold.
Thus has it been taught in brief; what else do you wish to hear? (24)

Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Description of the Purification of the Elements," in the second section of the northern part of the *Śrīśaktisaṅgama-mahātantrarāja*, within the dialogue between the illustrious Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā. 12.
The Thirteenth Chapter.
The Lord said: "In the Kaula and Avadhūta paths, one should not undertake a pilgrimage to sacred sites."
Pilgrimage to sacred fords, renunciation, and the observance of vows as well.
One should entirely avoid fasting and shaving the head;
since the full consecration (pūrṇābhiṣeka) is upon the head, there is no shaving there.
The Kaula sacred sites (tīrthas) are divided; one should always dwell there in the Kaula [tradition].
O Goddess of the Gods, all the seats (pīṭhas) exist entirely within this one alone.
That sacred seat (pīṭha) would be the preeminent seat (*adhipīṭha*), for it possesses supreme sovereignty.
The Goddess said: "O Lord of Gods, I desire to hear about the Kaula pilgrimage sites (*tīrthas*) in their entirety."
Īśvara said:
Brāhmaṇī is declared to be Gayā, and the King (Kṣatriyā) is celebrated as Ayodhyā;
Vaiśyā is declared to be Avantikā, and Śūdrā is remembered as Mathurā. || 5 ||
O Goddess, Dāsī is considered Māyāpura, and Naṭī is regarded as Godāvarī;
O Goddess, Mālākāriṇikā is proclaimed to be Citrakūṭa.
The goddess Kumbhakāriṇī is proclaimed as Śrīpura;
O Great Goddess, Uḍḍiyāna is Saucikī and Pauṇḍravardhana.
Jālandhara is Kuvindā, while the weaver is Kāñcikā;
O Goddess, Asimārjanikā is remembered as Kāmarūpa.
The washerwoman’s [abode] is declared to be Puṣkara; the leather-worker’s is Kāśikā;
and the blacksmith’s house, O Goddess, is remembered as Kolāpura.
O Goddess, the house of the vintress is celebrated as Nepāla;
O Queen of the Gods, the seat of Kedāra is proclaimed as Nāpitī. (10)
O Goddess of gods, Gokarṇa-pīṭha is proclaimed as belonging to Tvaṣṭṛ;
Ujjayinī shall be the pīṭha known as Kalādika.
Kāleśvarī was a female attendant, Kaivartī was at Hastināpura,
Śaulkikī was at Rājageha, and Jayantī was an oil-maker.
Kānyakubja is Māgadhī; the application of the house [mantra] is everywhere.
Prayāga is the house of the courtesan (veśyā), while Śrīśaila is Kumārikā. 13.
The seat of Kailāsa is Ābhīrī; Kṣīrikā becomes Puṃścalī. O Goddess, the city named Hiraṇya is proclaimed to be Svairiṇī. (14)
O Goddess of Gods, Aṭṭahāsa, Sairandhrī, Dūtikā, Maruteśvara, Oṃkārapīṭha, and Raṇḍāgṛha are thus proclaimed. (15)
The house of a neighbor is declared to be the Pīṭha of Malaya;
the house of one's own wife, O Goddess, is declared to be the Virajā-pīṭha.
O Goddess, the house of the Kuṭṭanī is called Pūrṇacandra;
O Goddess, the house of Śrīgāruḍī is the sacred seat (pīṭha) known as Devamātṛka.
The sacred seat (pīṭha) of Āmrātakeśvara is said to be the house of the Cāṇḍālī;
Kāmakoṭa is the house of the granddaughter, and Ekāmbara is considered the house of the great-granddaughter.
The house of the maternal aunt is Ananta; that of the female artisan is Carasthira.
O Goddess, the house of the king’s daughter is celebrated as Māhendra. (19)
O Great Goddess, the Kanyāgṛha is called Jaleśvara;
O Maheśānī, the Snuṣāgṛha is celebrated as Vicitra. (20)
O Goddess, the house of one's sister is called Bhṛgupīṭha;
O Goddess, the house of one's sister-in-law is called Mahāpatha. (21)
O Goddess, a Yavanī woman, as well as Merukā and Girirevā, have been mentioned;
the house of a maiden who has already been married is known as Vāmana.
The house known as Hiṅgulā shall indeed be the abode of the auspicious Key to the Play;
the woman of another's family shall be the Viṇdu-tīrtha, and she in her menses shall be the Sarva-tīrtha.
All those holy places [are attained] by bathing even once at the confluence of the Mātaṅgī;
this has been declared, O Great Goddess. What else do you wish to hear?
The Goddess said:
"O Lord of Gods, I wish to hear the characteristics of the four seats (catuṣpīṭha).
Śrī Śiva said:
And I shall proclaim the secret, by the knowledge of which one becomes immortal.
The wife of the brother-in-law has Kurukṣetra as her home;
O Goddess, the home of his daughter is known by the name Śrīgaurīmukha.
O Maheśānī, [these are] the young, beautiful woman, one's own wife, and one's sister; and her elder [sister], O Great Goddess, and so on in order from the younger [sister].
The eldest is Kelikuñcī, while the youngest is Keligehinī.
O Goddess of the Gods, hear now the four seats (pīṭhas) as they are uttered in sequence. (28)
O Maheśānī, Kurukṣetra, Gaurīmukha, Pañcabhadra, Kelikuñcī, Mhinī, and Pañcabhadraka; (29)
Indeed, attending their assembly, reciting hymns of praise, bowing down in their company,
associating with them, worshipping them, being delighted by their words, and offering handfuls of flowers and so forth— these are proclaimed as the primary [forms of devotion]. (31)
One should unite desire with that which abides in desire and is situated in the midst of desire, and is encapsulated by desire; one should unite desire with desire, and desire with desire. || 32 ||
The sequence of the stages of worship (*pūjāvaraṇakrama*) is repeated again and again;
that conversation and that assembly—this is proclaimed here as "worship" (*pūjā*). (33)
The yantra is said to be a triangle; O Supreme Goddess, that which is situated therein is the dismissal (visarjana), the casting of the seed-syllable (bīja), and its worship from the hand.
Then that union is that Brahman; it is the kissing of the hands.
Having performed that [union] above and below, a man becomes one who is united with That. || 35 ||
O Maheśvarī, for him who performs the union of the four seats (catuṣpīṭha-samāyoga), O Goddess, you are pleased; there is no need for deliberation on this point. (36)
O Pārvatī, having carefully placed that upon its seat and into its mouth, one should perform the recitation while licking it; thus one shall become a master of all supernatural powers (siddhis).
One should always satisfy Kālikā through the yoga of the nectar of the triangle;
eloquence and poetic skill shall always abide in one's hand. (38)
O Pārvatī, having carefully beheld that wheel joined with flowers, O Goddess, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times; thus one shall become a master of all siddhis.
Having come together in union, they should perform the recitation during the four watches of the day;
or they may do so as available, whether it be a sister or a co-wife.
She who possesses the key to the secret (kelikuñcī) is especially pure; such a woman is particularly excellent.
He who acts in this sequence attains all accomplishments (sarvasiddhi). || 41 ||
"Thus has it been briefly proclaimed; what else do you wish to hear?
The Goddess said:
O Maheśvara, the four seats (catuṣpīṭha) have been described by you in brief. (42)
"Tell me the true nature of the power of the *pīṭha* (seat), as well as its secondary forms (*anukalpa*).
Śrī Śiva said:
A woman is the mother of the three worlds; a woman is the embodiment of the three worlds. (43)
Woman is the support of the three worlds; woman is the very embodiment of the body. Man is the form of woman, and whatever form is most excellent [is likewise her form]. (44)
Whatever form exists within the world, it is all contained within the circle of women;
there is no happiness equal to that of women, nor is there any destiny equal to that of women.
There has never been, nor will there ever be, fortune equal to that of a woman;
there is no kingdom equal to a woman, and no asceticism equal to a woman. 46.
There has never been, nor will there ever be, a sacred ford equal to a woman;
there is no yoga equal to a woman, and no recitation equal to a woman. 47.
There has never been, nor will there ever be, a yoga equal to that of a woman;
there is no mantra equal to a woman, nor is there any austerity equal to a woman. 48.
There has never been, nor will there ever be, any wealth equal to a woman—a young, beautiful, and charming lady whose mind is exalted by youth. (49)

Having brought such a beloved— one intoxicated with passion, with squinting eyes, always full of longing, adorned with all ornaments, sixteen years of age, and of this very nature— he should perform everything as before. (51)
O Supreme Goddess, having placed [the deity] upon a couch of flowers and having worshipped with all the ritual offerings (*sarvopacāra*), [one should perform] the recitation and so forth.
Having diligently worshipped Kālī together with her limbs (aṅgas) and her retinue (āvaraṇas),
one should, having become oneself unagitated, bring about agitation within her.
Whatever word is spoken by her shall come to pass exactly so;
by the touch of her body, this entire world of moving and non-moving beings is purified.
O Maheśānī, one should practice that same disposition within her house; having visualized her in the form of a woman, one should contemplate that "Yoginī has been born. || 55 ||
One should meditate upon everything as being like a yoga; by that, one becomes a lord of accomplishments.
One should recite the mantra while meditating on the reverse; by that, one becomes a lord of accomplishments. || 56 ||
Having herself assumed the form of a woman, she, who was in her own true nature as a loving lady, [took] the collyrium for her breasts, the parting of her hair, and her bracelets as ornaments. (57)
Having performed everything within one's own body, one should practice that [ritual] upon her;
just as sexual union is enjoyed by a woman in the triangle. (58)
And by that woman, [the practice] should be performed preceded by dhāraṇā.
In such an excellent yoga, one should practice the yoga of initiation (dīkṣāyoga).
Everything attains fruitfulness through the grace of the Kālī-vidyā. || 60 ||
"It must be guarded, guarded, guarded with great effort!
Thus it has been taught in brief; what else do you wish to hear?"
The Goddess said:
By beholding [it] a thousand times, a human being becomes liberated;
by beholding it a thousand times, the vision of the deity is certain.
The four seats have been proclaimed; now speak of the meditation for their accomplishment.
Śrī Śiva said:
That which is the wife of the brother-in-law is proclaimed as Kurukṣetra;
and that which is the daughter of her is declared to be Gaurīmukha. (63)
That which belongs to Śālikā is called Pañcabhadra;
and she who is said to be his eldest wife is Kelikuñcikā here.

O Pārvatī, the four seats (catuṣpīṭhas) are: Svargadvāra, Kāmabila, the supreme Mahāpatha, and Vāñchāmaṇi as the fourth.
Up to the sixteenth year, the former is considered to be "Born of Merit" (Puṇyodbhavā);
up to the thirty-second year, it is considered to be the "Couch of Immortality" (Amṛtāndolikā).
Then, for a period of eight years, it is named Sudhāsāgara;
thereafter, for a period of ten years, it is named Ānandavrata.
Up to the sixteenth [chapter] from the beginning, there is that which is named Mahāsiddhimukha;
first, there are five seats (pīṭhas) according to the sequence of the Hiraṇyarāja.
O Maheśānī, listen now with care regarding that maiden:

If the Brahmāṇḍa indeed blossoms, it is proclaimed as the Catuṣkaka;
for thirty-two years, it is known as the Sāmrājya-guṭikā.
(54) Thereafter, until the age of eight, it is considered the "Couch of Bliss" (Ānandatūlikā). Then, until the age of ten, it becomes the "Lotus of Good Fortune" (Saubhāgyakamala). || 72 ||
Now listen, O Pārvatī, to the characteristics of the temple of Śrī Śaktikā;
it is a great imperial mandala extending up to sixteen [yojanas]. (73)
O Goddess, the Svārājya-maṇḍala follows immediately after that;
O Goddess, the Vairājya-maṇḍala is next, and from that comes the Sarvajña-pīṭhaka.
Up to the sixteenth [verse] previously, two [mantras] were taught for one desiring supernatural powers (ṛddhi);
these goddesses, who bestow all accomplishments, are proclaimed as those of Kelikuñcī. (75)
Up to the sixteenth [letter] from the beginning, it is named Viśvarūpa;
O Goddess, that which follows the sixteenth is named Ṣaṣṭisiddhi.
O Goddess, the thirty-second is named Sundarīmohana;
immediately after that, the one called Śrīkālīmohana is proclaimed.
If the *puṣpiṇī* yoga occurs when all four [planets] are in their respective flowers, and if there is *ruḍhi*, *jāti*, or *kriyā*, one should mutter the *adhirājādhipa* mantra.
The seats (pīṭhas) have been described here, as well as their forms, scents, and names;
O Goddess, one should bestow them with effort, either according to the sequence beginning with Parā or otherwise.
O Supreme Goddess, let this yoga be imparted even to a mere woman;
O Mistress of the Gods, the practitioner must be free from conceptual thought and have conquered his senses. (80)
Free from desire, anger, and the like, and devoid of pity and shame,
O Goddess of Gods, one should not allow the mind to be disturbed even by a perceived fault.
O Pārvatī, this has been performed by another;
it has been performed by oneself continuously for two, three, four, or five days. (83)
O Goddess of gods, even having known this, if one remains free from modification, such a person is non-conceptual (nirvikalpa) and fit for the path; it is not otherwise.
O Goddess Śivā, even if by the power of fate she should prove unfaithful,
one should nevertheless strive with effort to bring her satisfaction.
Otherwise, one shall become a denizen of hell; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
She alone is the creator of the world, the sustainer of the universe, and she alone is the causal sovereign.
O Goddess, who here is able to determine her?
O Goddess, whatever is performed by her takes the form of universal satisfaction. (87)
O Maheśānī, one who regards [her] thus certainly becomes a practitioner (sādhaka).
[She is] the great divine Kelikuñcī, endowed with all auspicious marks. (88)
One should always meditate upon and worship her who is joined with the nectar of youth; by means of the sequence beginning with *ka* and *ha*, one shall certainly accomplish everything. (89)
If she is endowed with fragrance and form, she may possess the nature of a Siddha, a Vidyā, or similar beings. || 90 ||
On the bed she is called Sundarī; in assemblies for sexual pleasure, Tāriṇī;

O Goddess, she is celebrated as Mahālakṣmī in the manifestation of the erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra);

The news of union is the world; Bhairavī is considered to be afflicted by sleep.

Śrī Mahādakṣiṇākālī is the sovereign leader of the great empire;

This has been stated in brief by Balāsiddhikālī;

Having thoroughly examined from the root to the end through the sevenfold yoga, [one should observe] the lips, the pair of eyes, the cheeks, and the region of the forehead. (97)

Kālikā is the bestower of boons upon him; there is no need for deliberation here.

The practitioner, devoted to his spiritual practice, becomes equal to the wish-fulfilling tree (kalpavṛkṣa).

[The symbols are] the fly-whisk, the solar disc, the triple-threaded cord, and the lotus. (103)

In the absence of all [these], the practice should preferably be performed with one's own wife;

Having arranged the ritual vessels, one should bring the articles for worship;

If that [practice] were to arise from the Matanga [Tantra], it would also be [described] first [therein];

O Goddess, whether by the power of fortune she is obtained or not obtained, [she should be] initiated, devoted to the deity, and devoid of pity and shame. (111)
O Śivā, having approached one who is devoted to japa, one should accomplish all [goals];

Having performed the cleansing of the hair, one should arrange the ritual services;
having performed the touching, one should perform the recitation (*japa*), which arises from worship. 113.
Having fully worshipped and meditated upon Kālī along with her limbs and her retinue, O Goddess of Gods, at the conclusion of the worship... || 114 ||
One should recite [the mantra] there according to the number [prescribed] and cause it to expand. O Goddess of Gods, one should certainly perform exactly what has been stated by her.
Know, O Goddess of Gods, that this is worship; one should practice the yoga as she has described. (117)
Having performed the yoga and having drawn the yantra there, O Goddess, licking all of that, one should perform the recitation with a mind full of bliss. (118)
Worship, recitation, the service of cows, libations, as well as sprinkling and the feeding of the twice-born—these always abide there. (119)
The breaking of the bed is proclaimed as worship; muttering is declared to be speech;
entry is the rite of fire-oblation (*homa*); and the offering of libations (*tarpaṇa*) is [the next stage]. (120)
Its washing is purification, and its sight is the feeding of the twice-born;
such is this supreme great seat known as Svayambhū. 121.
By the mere sight of him, whatever spiritual powers (siddhis) exist come of their own accord and undoubtedly enter into a state of servitude. || 122 ||

O Great Goddess, even if millions of heroic accomplishments (*vīrasādhana*) were performed by someone throughout the end of infinite ages, it would be equal to [the merit of] this [practice] performed in a single moment. 123.
Thus has been declared this supreme sādhana, which bestows the sixty siddhis;
it is proclaimed to consist of three thousand and five hundred and fifty-four [verses]. (124)
O Goddess, a thousand suns, as well as a hundred kalās, O Śivā,
and two hundred and five— this is declared to be the Nāyikā-kula.
This is a most profound secret, to be guarded like one's own private parts;
indeed, after one year he shall become a king—no doubt should be entertained in this matter.
He himself shall be the form of Kālī; no deliberation is required here.
Now, O Maheśānī, I shall describe from the beginning the sprout of youth.
O Śivā, there are one hundred and fifty-two [deities] in the pair consisting of the divine and the non-divine, according to the sequence beginning with Citriṇī.

O Goddess, let this be applied in due order; no hesitation should be felt here.
[One should know] the divisions of the seats of Sundarī, as well as the forests and the groves. (131)
One should perform the enclosure walls and the steps according to the distinctions of the heroines;
O Goddess, there are four heroines who denote [the positions] through their transpositions.
O Goddess of gods, O beloved, this entire universe resides within the body of a woman;
indeed, an infinite number of universes is clearly manifest within the body of a woman. (133)
(58) O Goddess, whatever exists in the world is of the form of woman;
by worshipping that form, all women are worshipped. (134)
O Pārvatī, the Mahāvidyās, the Yoginīs, the Mātṛkās, and all the deities indeed dwell in their respective appropriate places and seats.
Having understood everything from the scripture, one should apply it according to what is appropriate;
that which was previously stated here applies to the bound souls (paśus), while this very same [instruction] applies to the divine ones. 136.
Likewise, there is no distinction even among heroes regarding the divine hero;
through the union with all-encompassing knowledge, there is the circumambulation known as the Brahmāṇḍa.

that earth is the womb of power (śaktiyoni), and the three worlds are situated within that womb. 138.
O Goddess, the earth is proclaimed to be twofold: concealed and manifest. || 139 ||
Manifest, hidden, and of great merit—one should perform its circumambulation;
O Great Goddess, the circumambulation known as the Brahmāṇḍa is the most excellent of all. (140)
O Goddess, for the sake of even a single foot [of land], Paraśambhu Sadāśiva is present;
indeed, Śiva alone knows the abundance of fruit in this matter. (141)
O Goddess, by remembering or speaking [of this], the three worlds become honored;
it is declared that [this applies] to Śakti, whereas in the Śaiva tradition, there may be separation.
By the elision of this [anusvāra], the state of old age (vṛddhāvasthā) is proclaimed as "elision" (lopa).
Śakti is the garden of youth, and the navel is proclaimed as the "well" (kūpa). || 143 ||
O Maheśānī, desire is the door; likewise, O Śivā, there are the ten flavors.
O Supreme Goddess, she abides by means of the five locations of the eyes;
that Brahman which is the essence of aesthetic rapture (sāmarasya) is proclaimed to be the very Self. 145.
The sounding of that [instrument] is declared to be the resonance (dhvani); its aesthetic flavor (rasa) is an ocean of nectar. Its excitants (uddīpanas) are proclaimed to be fragrant scents. (146)
The *mānasam* is declared to be the *bhrāmaram*; the movements of birds are recorded [as distinct], while the movements of the various species of deer, cattle, and so forth, are proclaimed by others.
The *rāgas*, *tālas*, and *rāgiṇīs* constitute their conversation;
and all the *hāvas*, O Goddess of Gods, are considered to be the uprooting and replanting [of the seed]. (148)
The permanent emotions (sthāyibhāvas) are the sprinkling [of water], while the determinants (vibhāvas) are the gazing;
the movement from one place to another is proclaimed as the consequents (anubhāvas). || 149 ||
The garland-maker is Spring; side-glances are considered the flowers of the god of love.
A single, double, or triple row [of these glances] is considered to be like a newly-wedded bride, a mature woman, and so forth. (150)
The breaking of the garland signifies pride; its bending indicates the hero. Flowers such as the *mālatī* and others become the laughter of Rati. || 151 ||
Having thus understood everything, including the five types of fragrance and so forth, O Śivā; || 152 ||
O Maheśānī, that quality (dharma) is here proclaimed as Māyā;
its manifestations are proclaimed as grace, anger, and the curse. || 153 ||
Contentment is declared to be clarity, while censure is proclaimed to be agitation;
indifference and aversion are proclaimed to be the forms of power (śakti). (154)
The Āgneyī [path] is said to lead to heaven, while the Saurī leads to the world of men. || 155 ||
The lunar [element] is the netherworld; the three worlds are in the center of the corner;
the nature of the point (bindu) is Parjanya; all this is considered in brief. (156)
Sleeping, playing, eating, poetry, contemplating her form, whatever poetic conversations there may be, and all songs and poems; (157)
These are portions of the high-souled Viṣṇu, who assumes the form of sound;
what more need be said? The three worlds would become composed of him again and again.
The twenty-four musical instruments and the sound of their combination, as well as the drawing back of the hands, constitute the *mūrchanā*; [this is] liberation, O Śivā. (159)
O Maheśānī, it has been declared that heaven and liberation consist of entering [the Self];
for the ignorant who partake in suffering, liberation is considered to be exiting elsewhere. 160.
O Goddess Śivā, from knowledge of this, the fruit born of saṃsāra arises;
O Mistress of the Gods, even from ignorance it bestows fruit in this very same way. (161)
O Maheśānī, by knowledge alone—what is there that is not held in the hand?
There are thirty urvudas, six padmas, five vṛndas, and arbudas.
For one endowed with wisdom, initiation, and so forth, knowledge shines forth.
Through that knowledge, even a worm is liberated; O Pārvatī, hear now of that yoga.
O beloved, having previously been a worm, the living being perceives a bee; through the power of that perception, the state of being a bee arises. (164)
Furthermore, O Goddess, one who has attained the state of youthfulness does not become a worm;
for the meditation on the void, O Goddess, results in a form that is void and indeed devoid of essence.
O Goddess of the gods, as it is so, the yoga of contemplation (*bhāvayoga*) is the cause here;
for the Power (*śakti*), whose form is the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*), has the Supreme Brahman as its very nature. (166)
The power of consciousness (cicchakti) is the knower; its corner is the void (śūnya), from whose mouth have emerged bees numbering infinite crores.
One should thoroughly practice the true existence of that [reality] which has the nature of the Supreme; for this supreme state, or even the conscious Puruṣa, is easily attained. (168)

And he is declared to be the very form of Śiva; O Maheśvarī, through the yoga of contemplation, there arises the initiation of intelligence (*medhā-dīkṣā*), which is the most excellent among all. (169)
First, Kāmakalā is proclaimed; therein lies the Cintāmaṇi.
Then follow Bālā, the Sparśamaṇi, Kāmeśī, and Siddhakālikā. (170)
The sixteenth Vidyārājñī, Paśyantī, Kāmakālikā, Caraṇeśī, Haṃsakālī, and she who has the form of four feet. || 171 ||
One should perform the initiation of Medhā for both Kubjikā and Guhyakālī;
O Maheśvarī, the initiation of Medhā is said to be taught according to the sequence in both cases.
He who is initiated during the Dvūtūta period shall be known as Mahāmedha;
having previously been a living insect, he attains the state of a Bhṛṅga.
Then, having effected the union of the six cakras, one should become a consumer of that essence,
O Great Goddess, when the seat of the yantra has been established during each respective yoga.
By that [means], O Goddess, one should write down the mantras and perform their recitation;
through that, one becomes identical with the form of the mantra—this is proclaimed as Sāmrāṇmedhā.
The power itself and that pair [of Śiva and Śakti] arise through the union of their own respective sequences:
as Śaiva and Śākta, and as Śakta and Śaiva, through the union of those two sequences. || 176 ||
Having understood the wheels according to the stated path, O Pārvatī, and having pierced through the wheels, one attains that very nature which is their true nature. (177)
Neither the state of being a worm nor that of a bee exists by its own nature; rather, through the manifestation of the deity's form, one attains that very form in an instant. (178)
Indeed, that which is called Ardhanārīśvara is proclaimed as the Upper Yoga (ūrdhvayoga);
this one called Brahmanārīśvara is proclaimed as the Great Yoga (mahāyoga). || 179 ||
Then, O Śivā, the initiation known as the Divine Imperial Sacrifice (divyasāmrājyamedha) was proclaimed;
it is divine in form, of celestial form, the very form of mantra, and supreme among the great. (180)

This initiation, which possesses all forms and is foremost of all, endowed with the sacrifice of the great empire, has been proclaimed by me; one should protect it like a secret drop in the Kali age. 181.
O Goddess, after this initiation there is no other initiation anywhere;
Śiva knows it as half, while Kālī knows it in its entirety. (182)
In Guhyakālī, all this [is present], and from her comes Kubjikā Sundarī; O Goddess, everything beginning with the letters Ka and Ha is established therein. (183)
The Great Vidyā of the nine principles is the supreme Mistress of the nine wheels;
one who is endowed with initiation into this is proclaimed as a Keralī. 184.
From Cakṣuṣmatī up to this point, the sixtyfold Keralī possesses the supernatural powers (siddhis).
The power ending with Medhā has been described; it is joined with sovereignty and consists of salutation (namas). 185.

One who is connected with the peripheral [teachings] of the Cakṣuḥ [tradition] and possesses the realization of reality according to the Kāśmīrī [system], up to the full initiation beginning with the eyes, is designated as Gauḍa. (186)
The Lord of the Eight Siddhis is proclaimed; O Goddess, one should employ the vessels for worship according to the appropriate application of the digits (kalās) within the moon. 187.
Or else, O Supreme Goddess, in the Gauḍa tradition there is the visualization of poverty;
Śakti is said to consist of intelligence, and one should practice union with her. (188)
O Maheśānī, this divine yoga has been proclaimed before you;
it applies likewise to the divine wheel, the wheel of life, and the Śāligrāma stone. (189)
O Maheśānī, in the case of a Bāṇaliṅga, there is neither invocation nor dismissal;
these deities remain forever present in their manifest forms. (190)
In fire, in the midst of a lamp-flame, in water, and even in a mirror;
in the solar disc, in the lunar disc, and in Śāligrāma stones. || 191 ||
O Goddess of the gods, one should always worship [the deity] after invoking it within a crystal [yantra];
for the yantra is said to be the house, and the bindu becomes the throne.
The Śāligrāma becomes the temple; the collection of discs is the pedestal.
One should contemplate [the deity] as being joined with the disc, in the middle of the disc, or in its absence, above it. (193)
Whether it be a liṅga made of stone, crystal, diamond, or emerald, one should then visualize [the deity] upon it and worship Śiva with great effort. (194)

At Śāligrāma, one should worship the wheel of living beings (jīvacakra), which comprises all the gods; for whatever disposition is proclaimed for each [deity], it abides by means of that very disposition. (195)
Having placed a single flower, one should worship the Supreme Goddess;
for whatever yantra is joined with the seed-syllable (bīja), that yantra is the very form of spiritual accomplishment (siddhi). || 196 ||
O Śivā, having established either a śāligrāma or one of the yantras, when the divine wheel is attained, the wheel of the living being is no longer [present]. 197.
When the *jīvacakra* has been obtained, one should not worship the Bāṇaliṅga;
when the Bāṇaliṅga has been obtained, one should certainly not [worship] the Śāligrāma. (198)
When the Śāligrāma has been obtained, one should not worship elsewhere;
likewise, one should not worship both the Śāligrāma and the mantra in the same place. (199)
If one belonging to the fivefold lineage always worships the second [deity], he who performs a separate worship on a single seat creates a lute-like machine. (200)
He incurs the curse of the deities and shall go to the Raurava hell,
O Maheśvarī, even when a Śāligrāma or a yantra is present.
O Goddess, where does the Lord reside? There are two places:
the Śāligrāma is the sacred diagram (yantra), and the Śāligrāma is the abode (gṛha). || 202 ||

The yantra is said to be the house, and the deities are considered to reside within the house; or else, an image should be fashioned according to the prescribed rules, possessing auspicious characteristics. (203)
O Maheśānī, [the Lord] becomes pleased instantly in the Śāligrāma as well as in the Yantra;
in the Jīvacakra, however, He remains perpetually gracious.
In the Kali age, one who understands the wheel of life is indeed difficult to find; it would be like oil from sand, or as if a barren woman were to give birth to a son. (205)
Even a sky-flower might come into being, or even a man might be born from no womb;
but in the Kali age, there shall certainly never be one who possesses knowledge of the living wheel (jīvacakra).
Abandoning its foremost station, the foolish mind wanders for alms;
likewise, having abandoned the living soul (jīva), it runs and rushes about.
Oh, O Maheśvarī! A man who possesses this knowledge becomes equal to Śiva; he is so even while seeing, tasting, touching, [smelling], worshipping, and meditating.
O Supreme Goddess, the man who recites this becomes equal to Śiva;
he should unite the individual soul with the Life-force, and he should join the Life-force with the Life-force.
By uniting the individual soul with the Universal Soul, a man becomes liberated while living;
O Goddess, a supreme man who possesses the wheel of life is more blessed than the most fortunate.

O Goddess, he who knows the Supreme Self becomes one whose nature is bliss, whose nature is wealth, whose nature is knowledge, and whose nature is higher consciousness; he is the beholder of the living soul in a single moment. (211)
Holding the wheel of life (jīvacakra) in his mouth, Vādirāja recites the mantra a hundred thousand times;
O Goddess, Kālikā recites it a hundred thousand times with its essence.
Having offered one's tongue [to the deity], one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times; one will then become a bestower of power.
Having beheld [the deity], one should recite it one hundred thousand times; the practitioner will become a supreme poet.
Thus has it been briefly declared; what else do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "The Determination of the Kaula Tīrthas," in the second section of the northern part of the *Śrīśaktisaṅgamamahātantrarāja*, within the dialogue between the venerable Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā. || 13 ||
The fourteenth chapter.
The venerable Goddess said:
"O Lord, tell me now the sequence of worship for Śakti."
Śrī Śiva said:
I shall proclaim the worship of Śakti, by which one becomes identical with the Goddess.
An actress, a Kāpālikā ascetic woman, a courtesan, a washerwoman, a barber’s wife, the daughter of a garland-maker, and the daughter of a potter. (2)
This group of eight maidens has been declared; now hear of the eight families: the royal courtesan, the secret courtesan, and likewise the divine courtesan. (3)
Dancing, processions, sacred fords, prostitutes, and procuresses—these five destroy a prostitute; ten [such acts] destroy a mistress of the house.
When twenty-five [syllables] are joined together, she is proclaimed as Tuṣṭā;
when fifty [syllables] are joined together, she is proclaimed as Siddhā. || 5 ||
A hundred Nandas and a thousand Sundaris,
joined with innumerable [attendants], are considered to be devoted to Brahman.
Now, O Pārvatī, listen to the eight families (kulāṣṭaka) according to their true nature; O Maheśānī, in the center is the most excellent great garland.
O Goddess, you are the source of the universe, the womb of all, and superior even to everything; in the group of eight Kulākulās, you are proclaimed to be twofold.
In Gauḍa, the pair consisting of a queen, a courtesan, and so forth, is the service of flowers;
likewise, [the pair] consists of mother, daughter, granddaughter, sister, daughter-in-law, and younger sister.
The sister-in-law, the playful key, and likewise the mother’s wife as the eighth—
this is declared to be the group of eight kulas, which bestows all accomplishments.
A young woman, beautiful, charming, restless, and longing, who is devoted to her guru, endowed with the power of mantra, and possessed of all auspicious marks. (11)
Having brought [the woman] into such a state upon a bed of flowers, the repeated movement back and forth is declared; this is known as the "Laughing Flower" (Puṣpaprahasita).
Speech is declared to be *japa*, while its recitation is considered the best;
anger is declared to be restraint, and the taking of the hand (marriage) becomes fearlessness.
(65) Spreading one's feet upon the earth is the circumambulation;
placing one's foot upon the neck is declared to be the lion-throne.
When this is reversed, O Maheśvarī, it is called the worship known as the swing. 16.
The emission is the casting of the seed-syllable, while the mudrā is the embrace;
O Goddess, this is declared to be the Khecarī-yoga involving the lips. (17)
O Goddess, on the cheeks she is celebrated as Guṭikā;
O Goddess, on the forehead she is celebrated as Labakā. || 18 ||
O Goddess, that which is in the eye is proclaimed as collyrium;
O Goddess, that which is in the hand is proclaimed as the perfection of the sword.
Beholding the earth, however, shall result in the vision of the deities. || 21 ||
One should always associate with the virtuous; having beheld her, one should constantly recite [her mantra].
On one side, the gift of millions of universes and so forth is proclaimed. (22)
O Goddess, beholding its shadow would be the most excellent of all things;
it surpasses ten million holy fords of asceticism and even ten million sacrifices. (23)
O Goddess, he by whom an infinity of temples has been built continuously attains this vision of the one whose form is the Bindu.
O Goddess, the vision of Brahman is superior even to the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahman);
likewise, O Beloved, the nectar of the moon and the nectar of heaven [are surpassed] by the fear of Rāhu. (25)
Out of fear of the Rākṣasas, the nectar of the moon shines upon her upper lip, and the nectar of heaven, O beloved, resides upon her lower lip. (26)
O Goddess of the gods, it always abides; one attains success through knowledge, and not otherwise.
Through ignorance, it becomes like poison—there is no need for further deliberation on this point. (27)
In her mouth she holds wine and a rosary; her appearance is that of a temple.
In her heart is a fierce woman, yet in the courtyard of her house is a row of lamps.
O Goddess, how can that man who does not perform [this] be my worshiper? Such a conjunction occurs at the end of a great kalpa, O Goddess.

Just as an eclipse of the sun is an unfavorable conjunction when the moon is in opposition, so too one who is negligent, whether by mind or otherwise, does not wear the rosary even if it has been consecrated. (30)
O beloved, one should cause her to utter whatever words she speaks;
likewise, when the yoga has been commenced, one should not speak of "full yoga."
If it has not yet arisen for a person, he plays with it repeatedly;
however, when he is swallowed by it, he should be known as one who has transcended all the most excellent of joints (parvan). || 32 ||
When one has personally begun the practice, having first [prepared] for oneself...
by performing the task in that manner, no downfall occurs for him. (33)
That [conjunction] should be known as "eclipsed at rising," which bestows all siddhis.
This supreme secret has been declared; now listen, O beloved, to the yoga of the day.
The Ardhodaya (Half-Rising) of that [Tithi] is considered to occur in its own sequence;
Mahodaya occurs in its own conjunction, while Vārtā is remembered as the Daśaharā.
The third is proclaimed as the one called Akṣayarūpā, which consists of news of that [place].
Thus it has been briefly told; hear now the specific details, O Pārvatī. (36)
O Goddess, the twelve months have been proclaimed in their proper sequence; O Maheśānī, when conjoined with the seasons, they are said to constitute the Great Sovereignty.
This has been declared regarding the divine [beings] and others; now listen, O Pārvatī, concerning the bound souls (paśus):
O Goddess, during an eclipse of the sun or moon, [the distance] is two finger-breadths and more.
The tantrikas maintain that it increases by two and a half finger-breadths;
during a solar eclipse it lasts for four watches (yāmas), and during a lunar eclipse it shall be three watches.
O Maheśānī, piercing (vedha) has been described; it is the piercing of the sight of the two preceding [asterisms].
O Devī, one must not eat there, but should perform bathing, giving of gifts, and other such rites.
O Maheśvarī,
having observed through the perspective of the scriptures both the eclipsed sunrise and the eclipsed sunset, one should perform bathing, giving gifts, and other such rites.

Having diligently understood everything—when [there is] bondage and when there is liberation—one should perform bathing, giving, and other rites; otherwise, it is not so, according to the word of Śaṅkara.
One whose son is living should never observe a fast;
for one who has first seen the sun eclipsed and then released it, fasting is not prescribed. (43)
When the sun rises while already eclipsed, one must never eat during the preceding period of overlap;
yet here, some who are like beasts, deluded by the scriptures, maintain that it is permissible. (44)
(67) O Supreme Goddess, one should observe a fast when [the sun] is eclipsed by Rāhu;
the vision of the scripture is the manifestation [of truth], while its direct perception is its state of fullness. 45.
O Queen of the Gods, even for the divine beings, it shall be two finger-breadths;
however, for the devotees of Śiva, a fast of three nights is prescribed. (46)
For the Vaiṣṇavas, Gāṇapatas, and Sauras, a two-night period is prescribed;
for the Śāktas, however, it should be the first part of the night, provided they are engaged in the preliminary ritual service (puraścaryā).
O Goddess, this has not been taught by me to those who have not performed the preliminary rites (puraścaraṇa);
however, in the Cāndra-Svāyambhuva [tantra], it is proclaimed as lasting for two nights.
Wherever there is a pair of occasional rites, there the expression of desire is minimal;
thus has it been briefly declared. Now hear the fruit of the tradition. (49)
The Kerala, the Kāśmīra, and the Gauḍa as the third—
these are declared to be the three traditions that bring about all spiritual accomplishments.
Knowledge that is correctly imparted is proclaimed as *sampradāya* (the tradition);
it is free from defects such as desire and the like, and its Lord is the Master of the Kādimata. || 51 ||
The desired accomplishment is thus fashioned from one's heart's desire;
O Goddess, it becomes like another jewel in the world, possessing all sovereignty.
Having wiped away the lines on the forehead, one should fashion them anew,
endowed with the great mantra of the rays of knowledge and the circle of mantras.
The Lord of the Great Vidyā-maṇḍala, endowed with the sovereignty of the maṇḍala,
is described as consisting of eight times eight [parts] and is accompanied by the five pārāyaṇas.
It shall consist of the Śāmbhava questions and so forth, be endowed with the four junctions (saṃdhyās), and be accompanied by the five recitations (pārāyaṇas). || 55 ||
It is joined with the Wish-Fulfilling Creeper (Vāñchākalpalatā), named the Mantra-Maṇḍala;
it is endowed with the Great Vidyā and accompanied by the ten Pādukās. || 56 ||

O Goddess, even in the systems beginning with *ka* and ending with *ha*, that which is joined with the fivefold and sixfold [mantras] is such that the vital breath (*prāṇa*) and mind cause the movement of the *mūrti-sphoṭa* and so forth.
Laughing and shaking, he clearly utters speech from his mouth;
he who is the lord of the sixty siddhis is proclaimed as the Keralan. (58)
Listen to [the account of] Kāśmīra, O Goddess of Gods; be attentive in mind.
One who is free from miserliness and the like, and endowed with qualities such as the Vāmā, [should proceed]. (59)
Endowed with the yoga of both the upper and lower traditions (ūrdhvāmnāya), possessing the power to bestow sovereignty,
he is the lord of the twenty-four Siddhas and the most excellent among men.
(68) He who is joined with the single Upper Tradition (ūrdhvāmnāya) is proclaimed as Kāśmīra;
he who is joined with both Upper Traditions is called Mahākāśmīra. || 61 ||
Now, O Great Goddess, the Gauḍa [mantra] is being told; listen now.
It is one that converses with the hosts of gods and destroys the Gāruḍa and other [mantras]. (62)
That man who has reached the further shore of the illustrious Jñānasarasvatī is a hero who brings joy to the world, is devoted to women, and has conquered his senses.
O Pārvatī, he who is endowed with the kalās beginning with Ḍāmara, possessed of the complete initiation (pūrṇadīkṣā),
and equipped with the aforementioned authority, [is qualified] here as well as previously.
One who is joined with the eight groups of eight and so forth, who observes the conduct of the pledges (samaya),
and who possesses great strength and great enthusiasm, is designated as a Gauḍa.

The Gauḍa [style] is proclaimed to be of two kinds—Pūrvagauḍa and Madhyagauḍa—and it should be understood as being like the former; indeed, this Gauḍa bestows all supernatural attainments (siddhis). || 66 ||
The venerable Gauḍa is proclaimed as being endowed with the eight supernatural powers, beginning with atomization (aṇimā).
O Goddess, the prior distinction regarding the three lineages has been declared.
Devoted to the recitation of the Supreme Lord, endowed with compassion for all beings, a renouncer, an enjoyer, humble, and a constant worshiper of the Tithinityās. || 68 ||
O Maheśvarī, [the sins are] reviling others, malice toward others, slander,
[desiring] another's wife and another's wealth, and the sixth is indeed the acceptance of gifts.
One should indeed avoid all this; otherwise, the count would be one hundred.
[One should also avoid] malice, slander, the wealth of others, and accepting gifts. (70)
One should especially avoid the five reversals in the Śākta [tradition]. The doctrine of Vaṭuka has been declared; now hear the doctrine of Śaṅkara.
One should avoid the food of others and the hands of others in every way;
the hand of another is said to take away all merit, recitation, and worship.
Chanting another mantra while being intent upon other deities, he is estranged from the tradition and possessed of every fault. (73)
O Maheśvarī, in the Kali age, a man who is greedy and heretical is so described; whatever sin he commits, whether good or evil, [is his alone]. (74)
O Goddess of Gods, one who eats from his [the guru's] hand certainly obtains a portion of that [merit];
likewise one who subsists on food from a wall, one devoted to japa, one devoted to the guru, and one who has conquered the senses. || 75 ||
O Maheśānī, a man shall always become a speaker of truth;
endowed with virtues such as generosity and the like, he shall eat his food from his own hand. (76)
Especially, O Great Goddess, one should avoid the hand of a woman;
O Goddess, one should never engage in conversation with women or Śūdras. (77)
This has been declared for the Paśumatī [tantra], which was previously described as being among the divine [tantras].
Having brought forth the Śakti previously mentioned, who is endowed with all auspicious characteristics, || 78 ||

O Supreme Goddess, having diligently brought [the disciple] who is devoid of compassion, shame, and so forth, one should perform the entire series of ritual deposits (nyāsa) and other rites as previously described. (79)
One should worship with the perception of them as deities, free from all sense of modification.
While performing that ritual in the sacrificial pit, one should perform the recitation (japa) continuously.
There, having given [the offering], one should perform the recitation with undistracted mind.
Having reflected again and recited [the mantra] while remaining fully awakened, O Supreme Goddess, a man shall become a lord of all accomplishments and become equal to Śiva. (83)
The water issuing from his hand becomes equal to divine pearls;
it becomes a diamond, a crystal, a mantra, or gold.
Thus has it been briefly declared; what else do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Worship of Śakti," in the second section of the latter part of the *Śrī-Śaktisaṅgama-tantrarāja*, within the dialogue between the venerable Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā. || 14 ||
Fifteenth Chapter.
The Lord said: [This chapter contains] the description of the female form, the male form, and the application of the lattice-window (gavākṣa).
The knowledge of the Siddheśvarīs and others, characterized by the qualities of the wives of heroes and so forth. || 1 ||

O Goddess, regarding the families of the four castes and the four [orders], there is the description of the various sacred sites (tīrtha) resulting from their transgressions, and the determination of the sacred site of the courtesan. || 2 ||

Because of the courtesan-like nature and the infidelity of the fifty goddesses of the sacred seats; because of the courtesan-like nature and the infidelity of the fifty goddesses of the sacred seats. (3)
It is being told, O Goddess of the gods; be attentive in mind [to her who is] beautiful, youthful, delightful, lovely-limbed, and sweetly smiling.
Devoted to her guru, absorbed in japa, and filled with great passion and curiosity,
she was a virtuous woman who could enchant by her very sight and captivate with the casting of her glances.
She was intent on uprooting flowers, provided with hair-dyes and cloth-dyes, and endowed with the digits of the womb.

It was endowed with various skills in cooking and possessed excellent qualities such as foods to be licked and drunk; it was divine, delightful with its beds, and pleasing with mouth-fresheners and other such luxuries.
She was intent upon singing, keeping time, and playing the lute like a female bee;
she was endowed with poetic discourse, the composition of verses to be completed, and the like, as well as with sprouts and other offerings.
Endowed with various wonderful arts, possessed of loveliness, equal to the eight types of heroines, and free from anger and envy. || 11 ||
That which is devoid of all defects is proclaimed to be Śakti;
O Maheśānī, the nature of the Puruṣa is now being described—listen.
Skilled in various amorous sports, endowed with all powers, youthful, handsome, heroic, and a performer of deeds for a long time. (13)
He should be tall, firm in striking, and devoted to that [practice];
he should be skilled in the arts of the Kama-shastra and endowed with knowledge of mantras, channels, and medicinal herbs. || 14 ||

One who possesses the knowledge of the pillar (*stambha*), who is endowed with growth, stoutness, and long-lasting activity, who is devoted to the five forms of the letter *ma*, who is devoted to the Guru, and has conquered his senses; (15)
Constantly devoted to recitation at all times, he knows the true meaning and principles of all tantras, and is intent upon the practices of attraction, subjugation, and expulsion.

Endowed with both wisdom and discernment, free from defects such as desire, he was a preeminent leader among those skilled in singing, instrumental music, the lute and other instruments, as well as poetry and drama. || 17 ||
He was a knower of the sprouts [of truth], devoted to his lineage, and most excellent;
he was a master of the knowledge of the female form, as well as another who possessed knowledge of the body;
he was skillful in bestowing curses and favors, and was intent on compassion for all beings. || 19 ||
The knower of all the wheels, adorned with divine garments, endowed with divine ornaments, and possessed of every fragrance; || 20 ||
Always staying in the incense chamber, he was supreme in his knowledge of the three periods of time;
endowed with the knowledge of feminine forms, he always possessed their very nature.
O Maheśānī, one who possesses knowledge of riddles and treasuries and is endowed with the ability to delight the household— only such a person as this is worthy of the practice, and not otherwise.

Even there, O Maheśvarī, one who observes the *kālika-bhakta* (the practice of eating only at specific times) is indeed rare in the Kali age; having thus reflected upon these qualities, [He spoke] with a smiling face.
O Goddess, one should cause the sādhana to be performed; otherwise, it is not the word of Śaṅkara.
One who recites the mantra of the three powers (triśakti) in three ways should practice yoga at the window.

Having gone to a temple, on a riverbank, or to any pleasant place where the fragrance of incense pervades, one should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and other preliminary rites.
O Maheśvarī, having performed the sixfold ritual beginning with the Ṛṣi and Chandas and ending with the Kullukā,
and having meditated upon it, O Maheśānī, one should fix the gaze through the window.
Having clearly visualized [the path] from the big toe up to the crest of the head, one should perform the recitation;
likewise, one should visualize the solar disc as a bee and the confluence of the three rivers (Triveṇī) as a lotus pond.
O Goddess, [there are] the sesame flower, the wagtail, the campaka, and the kāmarūpaka; the nectar, the flowering [tree], as well as song and instrumental music. (28)
Having reflected, O Goddess, one should perform the recitation, especially in the abode of desire;
having reflected on the sequence from one, two, three, up to ten, one should carry out the recitation. (29)
Having seen a woman with flowers there and having respectfully formed a connection with her,
one should perform the recitation (japa) with undistracted mind by means of the power of the lattice-window connection.
O Goddess of gods, one certainly becomes capable of eightfold concentration; there is no doubt.
Alternatively, another method of practice is now described.
Having observed a young woman of noble birth, one should cause [the rite] to be performed;
thus one should do so for eight months, for it bestows success and not otherwise.
O Goddess of gods, one certainly becomes possessed of tenfold attentiveness (daśāvadhānī) and not otherwise;
having brought the wife of a hero, one should perform the rite upon the bed of a corpse.
Having diligently performed the *vīrasādhana* by means of a corpse,
and having secured access through a window, O Supreme Goddess,
if one recites [the mantra] for exactly one year there, O Goddess, that man shall become equal to Kālī.
O Goddess of the gods, such a supreme among men indeed becomes one who possesses a hundred-fold concentration;
or else, another method of practice is now described.
